title: Belgium – Company health services – La fourniture d’un service externe pour la prévention et la protection au travail (SEPPT).
description: La fourniture d’un service externe pour la prévention et la protection au travail (SEPPT), tel que prévu par la loi et le Code du bien-être au travail. Il sera fait appel au SEPPT pour la surveillance de la santé de notre personnel (y compris les attestations médicales et psychologiques dans le cadre de la réglementation ferroviaire), la gestion des risques (y compris les interventions psychosociales formelles), les visites des lieux de travail et d’autres services relevant des 7 domaines du bien-être prévus par la législation. Un élément important dans le cadre du présent marché est que la collaboration est également soumise à des dispositions légales spécifiques. Compte tenu de la nature et de l’ampleur des activités de la SNCB, l’accent de la future mission portera sur le volet médical, en particulier la surveillance de la santé. Environ 80 % des membres du personnel exercent une fonction de sécurité telle que définie dans la législation relative au bien-être, tandis qu’environ 50 % exercent une fonction de sécurité ferroviaire. Pour les fonctions de sécurité ferroviaire, telles que les conducteurs de train, les accompagnateurs de train et d’autres fonctions comportant des tâches critiques pour la sécurité, les attestations requises ne peuvent être délivrées que par un centre médico-psychologique agréé par le SSICF. Le futur fournisseur devra dès lors disposer d’un tel agrément ou être disposé à l’obtenir. En moyenne, environ 15 900 examens médicaux et psychologiques sont réalisés chaque année. Cela comprend notamment les examens périodiques, les examens spéciaux, les attestations médicales et psychologiques conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire, les examens préalables à l’embauche et les examens en cas de changement de poste de travail. Vous trouverez ci-dessous une indication du nombre des différents examens réalisés par an : Examens périodiques 8.500 / Examens spéciaux (consultations spontanées, RIT, visite préalable,…) 2.900 / Attestations médicales (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 2.700 / Attestations psychologiques (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 500 / Examens préalables (embauche + changement de poste de travail) 1.300 / TOTAL 15.900 / Étant donné que les activités de la SNCB sont réparties sur l’ensemble du territoire belge, le futur prestataire de services doit être en mesure d’organiser le service au niveau national, tant en néerlandais qu’en français. La préférence est donnée à une prestation de services dans les bâtiments de la SNCB ou dans des lieux situés à proximité d’un bâtiment de gare et/ou facilement accessibles en train. Une spécificité supplémentaire concerne la combinaison de membres du personnel statutaires et contractuels. Pour les membres du personnel statutaires, un statut spécifique et une réglementation du personnel spécifique sont applicables, à savoir le RGPS, ce qui suppose que le prestataire de services puisse aligner sa prestation sur ceux ci. En outre, l’intégration des données entre les systèmes du prestataire de services et SAP constitue une exigence dans le cadre de la future collaboration. Compte tenu de la complexité de la mission, de l’intégration, du besoin de continuité et de la sensibilité des données, il est actuellement envisagé de prévoir un marché d’une durée de 8 ans. Dans le cadre de la présente procédure de passation, la SNCB agit en tant que centrale d’achat au sens de l’article 2, 6°, b), de la loi du 17/06/2016 relative aux marchés publics, exerçant des activités d’achat centralisées et auxiliaires au sens de l’article 2, 7°, b), et ce pour les filiales de la SNCB, telles qu’Ypto.

title: Belgium – World wide web (www) site design services – Strategisch ontwerp, implementatie, migratie en ondersteuning van het nieuwe VIB-webplatform
description: VIB is een toonaangevend life sciences onderzoeksinstituut dat wetenschappers, technologie-experts en innovatieprofessionals samenbrengt rond één gemeenschappelijke ambitie: bijdragen aan een gezondere en duurzamere wereld door baanbrekend wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Met meer dan 2.000 onderzoekers, verspreid over verschillende onderzoekscentra op de Vlaamse universitaire campussen, behoort VIB tot de internationale top in life sciences onderzoek. Het platform ondersteunt uiteenlopende doelgroepen, waaronder onderzoekers, industriële partners, investeerders, beleidsmakers, journalisten, studenten, werkzoekenden en het brede publiek. Het vormt het belangrijkste digitale toegangspunt tot het onderzoek, de expertise, de dienstverlening en de impact van VIB.

title: Romania – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – ELABORARE STUDIU DE FEZABILITATE PRIVIND OBIECTIVUL DE INVESTITII „VARIANTA DE OCOLIRE A ORASULUI HARLAU, JUDETUL IASI”
description: Contractul vizează elaborarea Studiului de Fezabilitate obiectivului de investiții „VARIANTA DE OCOLIRE A ORAȘULUI HÂRLAU, JUDEȚUL IAȘI”, în județul Iași. Proiectul este strategic pentru decongestionarea traficului de pe DN 28B. Propunerea de traseu pentru Varianta de Ocolire Hârlău începe la intersecția cu DN28B – zona de sud a Orașului Hârlău și se termină la intersecția cu DN28B zona de nord a Orașului Hârlău cu o direcție orientată nord-est. Profilul transversal al aliniamentului se caracterizează printr-o lățime a părții carosabile de 12 m cu două benzi, câte o bandă pe sens (fiecare cu o lățime de 3.5 m). Intersecțiile cu infrastructura rutieră existentă se vor realiza prin sensuri giratorii. Obiectivul de investiții va fi proiectat și executat la un nivel tehnic și calitativ corespunzător unei infrastructuri rutiere moderne, respectând exigențele esențiale stabilite prin legislația în vigoare și normativele tehnice specifice drumurilor. Structuri rutiere și lucrările de artă vor fi dimensionate conform traficului estimat (straturi de fundație stabilizate, mixturi asfaltice adecvate pentru trafic greu, etc.), amenajarea elementelor de captare și evacuare a apelor pluviale, a taluzurilor și a zonelor conexe drumului. Se va asigura iluminatul public și semnalizare completă. Elementele componente ale viitorului contract: 1. Proiectare: • Elaborare Studiu de fezabilitate (Etapele 1–5); • Asistență tehnică acordată Beneficiarului pentru avizarea Studiului de fezabilitate în CTE și aprobarea indicatorilor tehnico-economici (Etapa 6). În conformitate cu prevederile art. 160 din Legea nr. 98/2016, termenele limită sunt stabilite după cum urmează: Operatorii economici pot solicita informații suplimentare/clarificari considerate necesare, privind documentația de atribuire cu cel târziu 25 de zile înainte de data limită pentru depunerea ofertelor, iar Autoritatea Contractanta va răspunde în mod consolidat tuturor solicitărilor primite într-un singur termen limită, stabilit cu 12 zile înainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor. Aceste termene au fost corelate pentru a asigura operatorilor economici timpul necesar analizei documentației și adaptării ofertelor în conformitate cu precizările furnizate de Autoritatea Contractantă.

description: La fourniture d’un service externe pour la prévention et la protection au travail (SEPPT), tel que prévu par la loi et le Code du bien-être au travail. Il sera fait appel au SEPPT pour la surveillance de la santé de notre personnel (y compris les attestations médicales et psychologiques dans le cadre de la réglementation ferroviaire), la gestion des risques (y compris les interventions psychosociales formelles), les visites des lieux de travail et d’autres services relevant des 7 domaines du bien-être prévus par la législation. Un élément important dans le cadre du présent marché est que la collaboration est également soumise à des dispositions légales spécifiques. Compte tenu de la nature et de l’ampleur des activités de la SNCB, l’accent de la future mission portera sur le volet médical, en particulier la surveillance de la santé. Environ 80 % des membres du personnel exercent une fonction de sécurité telle que définie dans la législation relative au bien-être, tandis qu’environ 50 % exercent une fonction de sécurité ferroviaire. Pour les fonctions de sécurité ferroviaire, telles que les conducteurs de train, les accompagnateurs de train et d’autres fonctions comportant des tâches critiques pour la sécurité, les attestations requises ne peuvent être délivrées que par un centre médico-psychologique agréé par le SSICF. Le futur fournisseur devra dès lors disposer d’un tel agrément ou être disposé à l’obtenir. En moyenne, environ 15 900 examens médicaux et psychologiques sont réalisés chaque année. Cela comprend notamment les examens périodiques, les examens spéciaux, les attestations médicales et psychologiques conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire, les examens préalables à l’embauche et les examens en cas de changement de poste de travail. Vous trouverez ci-dessous une indication du nombre des différents examens réalisés par an : Examens périodiques 8.500 / Examens spéciaux (consultations spontanées, RIT, visite préalable,…) 2.900 / Attestations médicales (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 2.700 / Attestations psychologiques (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 500 / Examens préalables (embauche + changement de poste de travail) 1.300 / TOTAL 15.900 / Étant donné que les activités de la SNCB sont réparties sur l’ensemble du territoire belge, le futur prestataire de services doit être en mesure d’organiser le service au niveau national, tant en néerlandais qu’en français. La préférence est donnée à une prestation de services dans les bâtiments de la SNCB ou dans des lieux situés à proximité d’un bâtiment de gare et/ou facilement accessibles en train. Une spécificité supplémentaire concerne la combinaison de membres du personnel statutaires et contractuels. Pour les membres du personnel statutaires, un statut spécifique et une réglementation du personnel spécifique sont applicables, à savoir le RGPS, ce qui suppose que le prestataire de services puisse aligner sa prestation sur ceux ci. En outre, l’intégration des données entre les systèmes du prestataire de services et SAP constitue une exigence dans le cadre de la future collaboration. Compte tenu de la complexité de la mission, de l’intégration, du besoin de continuité et de la sensibilité des données, il est actuellement envisagé de prévoir un marché d’une durée de 8 ans. Dans le cadre de la présente procédure de passation, la SNCB agit en tant que centrale d’achat au sens de l’article 2, 6°, b), de la loi du 17/06/2016 relative aux marchés publics, exerçant des activités d’achat centralisées et auxiliaires au sens de l’article 2, 7°, b), et ce pour les filiales de la SNCB, telles qu’Ypto.

Following launch, Government personnel will observe operational testing of the completed welding work. Background: Vessel identification: 47' MLB 47237 requires welding repairs on the port quarter. The work location on the vessel does not require certification by a marine chemist to gas-free the space. All materials required for the welding shall be sourced by the Government unit and provided to the Contractor prior to or at the time of work performance. This SOW defines the technical and performance requirements necessary to complete the haul-out, welding, launch, and support of operational testing. 2.2 Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all personnel, labor, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform Haul-Out, Welding, and Launch Services for the 47-Foot Motor Lifeboat (MLB) 47237 (Port Quarter Welding) as defined in this Statement of Work: Haul the 47' MLB 47237 out of the water using appropriate haul-out equipment and facilities. Perform welding repairs on the port quarter of the vessel in accordance with applicable welding standards and Government direction. Welding materials will be furnished by the Government. Upon satisfactory completion of the welding work, launch the vessel back into the water. Support Government observation of operational testing of the completed welding after the vessel is returned to the water. Due to the unit�s remote location, the vendor shall maintain a business location within 100 miles of the unit to ensure timely access, responsiveness, and continuity of support. Overland transportation of the vessel is not practicable due to its overall dimensions and weight. The vessel measures 47 feet 11 inches in length, has a 14-foot beam, a draft of approximately 4 to 4.5 feet, and a full-load displacement of 40,000 pounds. Its size, weight, and 5456 marine-grade aluminum hull construction create significant transportation, permitting, routing, and handling requirements. 2.3 Specific Tasks Task 1 � Pre-Haul Coordination (4.1) Coordinate haul-out schedule with the Government unit to minimize operational impact. Task 2 � Haul-Out Operations (4.2) Safely haul the vessel out of the water using Contractor facilities and equipment rated for the vessel�s size and weight. Position the vessel securely to provide safe and adequate access to the port quarter work area. Ensure the vessel is properly blocked, shored, or supported in accordance with industry best practices and facility procedures. Task 3 � Welding Work (4.3) Perform welding on the port quarter as directed by the Government unit using Government-furnished materials. Conduct all welding in accordance with applicable codes, standards, and good marine welding practice. Note: A marine chemist is not required to gas-free the work space due to the location of the repair area. Notify the Government unit upon completion of welding for inspection prior to launch. Task 4 � Launch Operations (4.4) Upon Government acceptance of the welding work, safely launch the vessel back into the water. Ensure the vessel is free of any temporary supports, debris, or equipment prior to launch. Task 5 � Operational Testing Support (4.5) Provide access and support as necessary for Government personnel to observe operational testing of the completed welding after the vessel is returned to the water. Remain available to address any issues related to the haul-out or welding process that may become apparent during initial operational checks. 2.4 Government-Furnished Materials (GFM) All materials required for the welding repairs shall be sourced by the Government unit and provided to the Contractor. The Contractor shall not be responsible for procurement of welding consumables, plate, or other repair materials. Government personnel have been afforded the opportunity to observe operational testing of the welding, and no defects related to the Contractor�s work are identified that require immediate correction. title: Y1JZ--926CM3010 Cemetery Expansion and FCA Improvements Project Washington Crossing National Cemetery
description: Market Research Only Not a Solicitation Notice purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), National Cemetery Administration (NCA), is conducting market research to identify capable, interested Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) prime contractors for a potential construction acquisition at Washington Crossing National Cemetery, 830 Highland Road, Newtown, PA 18940. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It is not a Request for Proposals, does not constitute a commitment to issue a solicitation or award a contract, and does not authorize reimbursement of response costs. Anticipated requirement The contemplated design-bid-build construction effort includes extensive excavation, grading, stormwater and utility infrastructure, roads, curbs, paving, irrigation and controls, columbarium construction, installation of approximately 8,500 Government-furnished pre-placed crypt units, and repairs/renovations to the Public Information Center and maintenance building. The design documents will identify approximately 4,080 columbarium niches. Facility work includes architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, envelope, and interior improvements. Construction will occur at an operating national cemetery; access, safety, visitors, and interment services must be accommodated. The period of performance for this particular project is estimated to be 12-18 months after the issuance of the notice to proceed (NTP). Government-furnished materials and contract interfaces Pre-placed crypt units will be procured by VA through a separate contract administered by the Memorial Products Service (MPS) and furnished for installation under the contemplated construction contract. The construction contractor will not purchase those units. Receiving, unloading, inspection, storage, handling, damage responsibility, and delivery coordination will be defined in the eventual solicitation. The procurement and furnishing responsibility for columbarium niche covers remains subject to Government confirmation. Estimated magnitude and acquisition approach The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $10M - $20M IAW VAAR 836.204(h)(1). The Government is considering a firm-fixed-price construction contract and a competitive SDVOSB set-aside, subject to market research and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. The anticipated NAICS code is 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction), subject to final determination. No final solicitation method, schedule, set-aside decision, or contract line-item structure has been established. Requested capability statement Interested firms should submit a concise capability statement, preferably no more than 12 pages, addressing the following: Legal business name, address, primary point of contact, email, telephone, UEI, CAGE code (if available), and website. Current SAM.gov registration and SBA VetCert SDVOSB certification status; identify any proposed joint venture and its members. Whether the firm intends to submit an offer as a prime contractor and whether it is a small business under the proposed NAICS code. Three to five relevant projects performed within the past ten years, stating customer, contract number (if available), prime/subcontract role, dollar value, scope, completion status/date, and point of contact. Highlight earthwork, stormwater systems, roads, precast installation, columbaria, and renovation of occupied facilities, particularly those with NCA. Available single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, supported by a surety letter if readily available; do not submit sensitive financial statements. Approach to managing simultaneous civil and building work, subcontractors, quality control, safety, scheduling, and work within active cemetery services. Experience receiving, coordinating delivery of, handling, and installing Government-furnished precast concrete products. Anticipated self-performed work and general approach to applicable limitations on subcontracting and similarly situated entities. Whether the combined project scope and proposed schedule are commercially practicable; identify meaningful competition barriers or recommended packaging alternatives. Any additional market information that would help VA develop a clear, competitive requirement. Response instructions Submit responses electronically to Auvorie Benson, Contracting Officer, via email at auvorie.benson@va.gov by November 9, 2026 at 8:00am EST. Use the subject line 36C78627Q0030_Sources Sought 926CM3010 Cemetery Expansion and Improvements_Washington Crossing NC. Identify proprietary information clearly. DO NOT SUBMIT A PRICE PROPOSAL. VA may contact respondents for clarification but is not obligated to do so. Disclaimer This is not a solicitation, prequalification determination, or request for quotations or proposals. Responses will be used to inform acquisition planning and market research. Failure to respond does not preclude participation in a future solicitation, if one is issued. Any future solicitation will be posted through SAM.gov. VA reserves the right to revise the requirement and acquisition strategy.

title: Velferdsteknologi for Nome og Midt-Telemark
description: Konkurransen gjelder levering av trygghets- og mestringsskapende teknologi som løpende tjenester, hvor valgt leverandør vil ha alt ansvar for integrasjon, overvåkning, support og drift av den totale løsningen, inkludert alle komponenter. Leveransene omfatter tjenester til hjemmeboende, institusjoner og bemannede boliger for både ansatte og tjenestemottakere. Det er også behov for å kunne kjøpe komponenter til løsningen, der hvor det er hensiktsmessig, for eksempel ved implementering av løsning til bruk institusjoner. Det er behov for at løsningen inkluderer en plattform for integrasjon . Oppdragsgiver har også behov for at det kan leveres responssentertjeneste for behandling av varsler, dersom det er formålstjenelig. Utrykning knyttet til oppfølging av brukere er ikke være en del av forespørselen. Deltagere i anskaffelsen: Nome og Midt-Telemark kommune Anskaffelsens verdi anslås til over EØS terskelverdi. Volumet er et estimat og er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. For nærmere informasjon viser vi til anskaffelsesdokumentene. Oppdragsgiver tar forbehold om avlysning av konkurransen, blant annet i forbindelse med budsjettmessig dekning. Plikten til å stille krav om lærling er vurdert til å gjelde for denne anskaffelsen, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5h. Se kontrakten for mer informasjon.

title: Replacement of the Perimeter Intrusion Detection System (PIDS) Integration Unit (PIU) and the Facility Alarm Annunciation System (FAAS) Integration Unit (FIU) at Mission Institution
description: This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Mission Institution in the Pacific Region. Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Competitive Procurement Strategy: compliant bid with the highest combined score of technical merit and price. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: This RFP is only for pre-qualified Suppliers against the Supply Arrangement (SA) Perimeter Security Management System and Interior Security Management System CW2440311 and CW2440314. The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Bosch Building Technologies Inc. • Vipond Inc. The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada requires the replacement of obsolete Electronic Security System (ESS) technologies within federal correctional institutions across Canada. The Contractor must provide the equipment, application software, process software, and associated services necessary to implement a modern Perimeter Intrusion Detection System (PIDS), Perimeter Security Management System (PSMS), and Interior Security Management System (ISMS). Objectives: To replace obsolete technologies that are well past the end of their service lives with a Perimeter Intrusion Detection System (PIDS) Integration Unit (PIU) and Facility Alarm Annunciation System (FAAS) Integration Unit (FIU) to form the core of the Command-and-Control requirements at Mission Institution in the Pacific Region. Deliverables: The Contractor must perform all tasks and provide the deliverables included in the following milestones: • Milestone 1: Project Initiation and Site Survey • Milestone 2: Design Approval • Milestone 3: Procurement and Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) • Milestone 4: Data Processing and Analytics Platform • Milestone 5: Installation and Cutover • Milestone 6: Acceptance Test Plan (ATP), Training and Closeout Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French). title: Wheel Force Transducers and Unmanned Ground Vehicle
description: The Department of National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of: 2.1. Four (4) wheel force transducers (WFTs), acquisition modules, and accompanying hardware The wheel force transducers are required by the NRC to conduct terrain sensing and vehicle mobility research in Arctic environments. 2.2. One (1) Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) for Offroad Robotics Research The required UGV will function as a configurable research platform for the development, integration, validation, and demonstration of technologies including autonomous navigation, localization and mapping, perception, sensor fusion, path planning, mobility in complex and unstructured environments, human-machine teaming, remote operations, edge computing, and other physical artificial intelligence and field robotics applications. The end result of this procurement will be the delivery of a complete, operational, research-ready UGV platform that can be integrated into the existing technology ecosystem developed and maintained by the Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAV) team of the NRC. This procurement has been set-aside under the federal government's Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Only Indigenous businesses as defined under PSIB are eligible to challenge the proposed procurement strategy to award the contract to the named Indigenous business.

title: Real Time Spectrum Analyzer
description: The National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of a 1.2 GHz acquisition bandwidth real-time spectrum analyzer (26.5 GHz) to capture and stream in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) data. The real-time spectrum analyzer will be used in a reverberation chamber to qualify DUTs against very stringent telescope protection levels. To achieve this, a low-noise, ultra-sensitive real-time spectrum analyzer is required. The real-time spectrum analyzer will capture and stream I/Q data that is used to reconstruct complex time domain signals that are then transformed to the frequency domain where radio astronomy techniques of spectral integration are used to reduce the standard deviation of the noise.

Only selected TBIPS SA Holders currently holding a TBIPS SA for Tier 1 in the Region: Virtual/Remote Access, under the EN578-170432 series of SAs are invited to compete. SA Holders may not submit a bid in response to this bid solicitation unless they have been invited to do so. However, should an uninvited SA Holder wish to be invited, it may contact the Contracting Authority to request an invitation at any time prior to five business days before the published bid closing date, and an invitation will be made to that SA Holder unless it would not be consistent with the efficient operation of the procurement process. One (1) contract will be awarded as a result of the evaluation of the responses to this RFP. Neither the qualifying proposal that scores the highest points nor the one that contains the lowest cost will necessarily be accepted. HICC reserves the right to accept any proposal as submitted without prior negotiations. Bids which fail to provide all information and documentation as requested in the RFP document by the time of bid closure will be declared non-responsive.

title: Specialist in Wargame Design and Facilitation
description: This re-solicitation is for the provision of a Specialist in Wargame Design and Facilitation in support of the Canadian Joint Operations Command's Exercise MAPLE LEAF PAJUK 2027.The work will include the following activities: Research, Design, Development, and Testing: From contract award through the pre-wargame phase, including the research, design, development, and testing of the wargame scenario and associated deliverables. title: VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) lisenssi- ja tukipalvelut
description: VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) lisenssi- ja tukipalvelut Hankinnan kohteena on Broadcomin VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) lisenssipalvelu (käyttöoikeuksineen) ja erikseen tilattavat tukipalvelut. Hankinnan kohde ja sitä koskevat vaatimukset on kuvattu yksityiskohtaisesti tässä tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. Tilaajana hankinnassa on Meidän IT ja talous Oy (Meita) ja sopimus tehdään kilpailutuksen perusteella valitun yhden toimittajan kanssa. Hankintasopimusta tulee käyttämään ainoastaan Tilaaja ja syntyvän sopimuksen osapuolina ovat ainoastaan Meita ja valittu Toimittaja. Selvyyden vuoksi todetaan, että Meitan asiakkaat eivät ole tämän kilpailutuksen tai sen perusteella tehtävän hankintasopimuksen sopijapuolia. title: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut
description: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta kotiin vietävistä ateriapalveluista seuraavien Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen kuntien alueella: Halsua, Kannus, Kokkola, Lestijärvi, Perho, Toholampi ja Veteli. Sopimus on määräaikainen ja voimassa kaksi (2) vuotta sopimuksen alkamisesta. Tilaajalla on lisäksi oikeus kahteen (2) erikseen päätettävään yhden (1) vuoden optiokauteen. Sopimuksen arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.2.2027. Hankinnan kohteena on kylmänä toimitettavat kotiateriat Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille. Kyseessä on sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014) 19 §:n mukainen tukipalvelu. Kotihoidon asiakkaat ovat pääsääntöisesti ikääntyneitä, joilla on usein alentunut fyysinen toimintakyky ja/tai muistin alenema ja jotka vielä pärjäävät itsenäisesti omassa tutussa elinympäristössään mm. ateriapalvelujen avulla. Asiakkaina on myös rintamaveteraaneja ja sotainvalideja sekä omaishoidontuen piirissä olevia asiakkaita. Hankittava palvelu sisältää aterioiden valmistuksen, kuljetuksen ja kaiken muun, mitä kyseiseen prosessiin liittyy. Hankittava palvelun määrä voi vaihdella sopimuskaudella. Sopimus ei sisällä Tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta. Hankinnan kohde on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.,

title: Call for Solutions - DeCA Stuttgart Area Commissaries Facility Maintenance
description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) maintenance services for the commissaries within the Stuttgart (Kelley, Patch, Panzer and Robinson) area. The prospective contractor shall provide a comprehensive preventative, unscheduled, and 24/7/365 emergency maintenance for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) services to ensure continuous operations and prevent inventory loss. Solutions should demonstrate rapid on-site emergency response capabilities, preventative maintenance compliant with local commercial standards, transparent fixed-price quoting and reporting procedures, and full compliance with applicable host nation (German/EU) statutory requirements and Department of War (DoW) statutory, safety, and warranty standards from firms operating in European Union, compliant with EU and host nation specific regulations and standards as it relates to commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) preventive maintenance and repair. Attached documents contain technical data that will provide assistance in understanding current conditions that the commercial solution will need to meet. Our objective is to establish a long term partnership with a provider whose technology, service model, and commercial terms align with our commitment to delivering reliable, value driven solutions. DeCA seeks solutions that will provide this support for up to five total years, requesting that solutions propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflect customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, use of CAFM systems, and repair benchmarks for the proposed support. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government's discretion. Please download the PDF documents attached to this call for solutions for additional details. The Call for Solutions Letter as five attachments on the PDF itself that contain important information to fully understand the complete nature of the call for solution.

title: Service Contract Renewal OXFORD INSTRUMENTS
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98027Q00045 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Oxford Instruments (Witec Instruments) for Service Contract for WiTec Raman Microscope Systems, Model: Alpha 300+, Serial No. 100-1200-2268. Description of the Requirement Service contract is essential for preventive maintenance, calibration and timely repairs of Witec Alpha 300R Raman microscope. Oxford Instruments Inc. (formerly known as Witec Instruments Inc) is the sole provider of genuine spare parts for these instruments and only qualified Oxford Instruments technicians can perform maintenance and repair of the equipment. A contract with a third-party repair/maintenance service will void Oxford service contract, and significantly increase the risk of disruptions in SPB/NICHD/NIH mission in the case of serious instrument failure. Contractor shall perform the following: PM � 1 Annual Preventative Maintenance (and/or Calibration) on-site Field Service Engineer Visit � covers PM parts, labor, travel expense. TECHNICAL SUPPORT �Access to Helpdesk and Technical Support included with priority response time during standard business hours Monday-Friday 8:30AM-5PM EST, excluding Federal Holidays. Technical Remote Support subject to connectivity and availability. LABOUR: Labor and Travel Expenses for all on-site FSE visits are included. PARTS � Includes replacement parts CONSUMABLES: consumables are not covered -however, a 10% OFF SILVER Contract discount applies towards all consumables via Oxford Instruments Online Store, Link to eStore: https://estore.oxinst.com/us SOFTWARE: Software fault or bug fixes are included. Software Updates are also included. Contractor shall provide OEM certified parts for all preventative maintenance and service repairs, except for consumables, at no additional cost to the Government. Shipping and handling parts under warranty or contract shall not be charged to the Government. Contractor shall provide an OEM service technician to perform all preventive maintenance inspections, service repairs and technical support. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Oxford Instruments Inc. is the manufacturer of the WTIec alpha300R Raman microscope and the sole provider of alignment and maintenance services currently deployed at the SPB / NICHD. As the manufacturer, Oxford Instruments maintains the proprietary hardware, firmware configurations, calibration specifications, replacement parts inventory required to support the WTIec alpha300R microscope. The WTIec alpha300R system, including its hardware, software, firmware, calibration and alignment processes, and supporting documentation, is proprietary to Oxford Instruments Inc. Maintenance services must be performed using manufacturer-approved procedures and replacement components to preserve compatibility with the existing hardware and software, and retain manufacturer support. To the Government's knowledge, no other vendor possesses the proprietary technology, replacement components, or integrated calibration/alignment capabilities necessary to provide maintenance services that are fully compatible with the existing WTIec alpha300R Raman microscope. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to Verne.Griffin@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 9, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00045 in the subject line of the submission.

Notes 1.0 INTRODUCTION The U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Dolphin (WPB-87354) requires commercial providers to perform cleaning of both Fuel Service Tanks. Maintenance Procedure Card (MPC) B24101.D 3.0 SCOPE OF WORK 3.1 The work is to be accomplished through the following: 3.1.1 Travel to work site / ship location: 1500 15th St. Mobile, AL 36615 3.2 Operational Test, Initial: Prior to commencement of work, the Contractor must witness Coast Guard Personnel perform an initial operational test of the designated tank level indicator(s) (TLI�s). 3.3 Tank Content and Waste Disposal: The Contractor must remove a total of 1400 gallons of contaminated diesel fuel. The Contractor must dispose of residual tank contents and any cleaning fluids in compliance with all applicable Federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, and regulations. Document a complete chain of custody record of the removed tank contents and generated wastes, from the vessel to the point of final destination or delivery. Provide any documents to the Coast Guard Inspector (EPO) upon completion. 3.4 Tank Cleaning Requirements: The Contractor must remove tank access cover(s) and clean tank interior surfaces free of all foreign materials, such as residual fuel or water, sediment, sludge, rust, or biological growth, taking care not to damage the coating system (if applicable). NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Call for Solutions - DeCA Bavaria Area Commissary Facility Maintenance
description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) maintenance services for the commissaries within the Bavaria (Grafenwoehr, Hohenfels and Vilseck) area. The prospective contractor shall provide a comprehensive preventative, unscheduled, and 24/7/365 emergency maintenance for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) services to ensure continuous operations and prevent inventory loss. Solutions should demonstrate rapid on-site emergency response capabilities, preventative maintenance compliant with local commercial standards, transparent fixed-price quoting and reporting procedures, and full compliance with applicable host nation (German/EU) statutory requirements and Department of War (DoW) statutory, safety, and warranty standards from firms operating in European Union, compliant with EU and host nation specific regulations and standards as it relates to commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) preventive maintenance and repair. Attached documents contain technical data that will provide assistance in understanding current conditions that the commercial solution will need to meet. Our objective is to establish a long term partnership with a provider whose technology, service model, and commercial terms align with our commitment to delivering reliable, value driven solutions. DeCA seeks solutions that will provide this support for up to five total years, requesting that solutions propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflect customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, use of CAFM systems, and repair benchmarks for the proposed support. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government's discretion. Please download the PDF documents attached to this call for solutions for additional details. The Call for Solutions Letter as five attachments on the PDF itself that contain important information to fully understand the complete nature of the call for solution.

description: See attached Sources Sought Notice and attached Draft Statement of Work. SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Solicitation Number: 75N98027R00005 Title: Quantitative Analysis of Longitudinal MR Images Classification Code/Title: AN11 - Health R&D Services; Health Care Services; Basic Research NAICS Code/Title: 541714 Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology) Size Standard: 1,000 employees Description: This is a Research and Development (R & D) Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential R & D requirement. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. Background: Since 1958, the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) has been a major research program conducted by the National Institute on Aging (NIA). The BLSA is a multi-disciplinary study of physiologic and psychological aspects of normal aging in community-dwelling men and women. Active BLSA participants are volunteers who visit the Clinical Unit of the NIA-Intramural Research Program (IRP) in Baltimore, MD for testing every 1 to 4 years. Since 1994, the NIA has been conducting a longitudinal brain imaging study of older adults in the BLSA to characterize individual differences in longitudinal brain changes, to investigate the extent to which these brain changes underlie individual differences in cognitive aging, to identify brain changes that may be predictors of cognitive decline and Alzheimer�s disease, and to assess the impact of potential modulators of brain and cognitive aging. As of October, 2024, more than 4000 neuroimaging evaluations have been performed for BLSA participants. As part of this research program, it has also been necessary to develop and validate sophisticated tools for analysis of longitudinal neuroimaging data that can be applied in large-scale studies. Thus, this project has involved the development, validation, and refinement of novel image analysis tools and the application of these tools to longitudinal Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging scans and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) measures of regional cerebral blood flow, amyloid and tau deposition in brain. More recently, these tools include advanced machine learning approaches using pattern analysis to classify clinical status and aging trajectories of individuals based on structural and functional brain images. The work of this requirement will continue to focus on the application of sophisticated tools and quantitative analysis of longitudinal MRI data acquired from BLSA participants. Thus, the proposed contract will apply methods developed in prior acquisitions, that allow continuity of research and provide longitudinal consistency of measures of global and regional brain volumes and ischemic lesion volumes, as well as functional MR data, including consistency with MR data acquired during earlier phases of this project (since 1994). This Contract will also require the application of sophisticated analytic approaches, including previously developed machine learning and pattern analysis methods, to allow classification of risk for cognitive impairment and likelihood of maintenance of cognitive resiience on an individual subject basis. Purpose and Objectives: The principal goal of this procurement is to provide quantification of MR imaging scans to provide measures of brain structure and function in BLSA participants, including heterogenous brain aging trajectories. Specifically, these data will allow NIA investigators to continue to address the following questions: What are the rates and regional distribution of changes in brain anatomy in non-demented men and women throughout adulthood? What is the frequency and progression of brain abnormalities in older adults and what is the clinical significance of these findings for cognitive aging? Against a background of age-related changes in brain structure, which changes predict cognitive impairment and Alzheimer�s disease, and conversely, what are the predictors of the maintenance of cognitive health or cognitive resilience? What factors modulate cognitive and brain aging and how do they impact brain-behavior associations? Project Requirements: See attached Draft Statement of Work.
